summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, and insulin therapy. Her elevated blood glucose and anion gap indicated diabetic ketoacidosis, which improved with hydration, though urinary ketones remained elevated. Hypertension and tachycardia, likely due to dehydration and vomiting, resolved with fluids and resumption of oral antihypertensives. She began tolerating small amounts of food but chose to leave against medical advice before completing monitoring for DKA risk. She was discharged with an updated insulin sliding scale, instructions to pre-treat meals with anti-nausea medications, and follow-up plans with GI and psychiatry.
